newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks close firm after Dow rebound.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks close firm after Dow rebound.

text.p: *Stocks ended firmer after the Dow's bounce on Monday with banks and media outperforming. Volume 366.9 million shares, value A$702.8 million, 1,084 stocks traded, 304 steady, 504 up, 276 down.
Australian shares closed firmer on moderate volume on Tuesday as investors factored in the strong recovery of the U.S. market.

The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, ended 22 points higher at 2,361.8, close to its intra-session high of 2,364.3. December share price index futures finished up 21 points at 2,355, a 6.8 point discount to the index.
Brokers said the market's gain was slightly disappointing given the Dow's 82 point surge on Monday and the 2.9 percent fall the Australian market suffered on Friday.

"There has been some quite large lines go through in some stocks which suggests people are happy to take big positions now but the volume generally was not extremely high," said Nick Atkinson, a dealer at Brisbane broker, Wilson HTM.

Banks dominated buying activity with ANZ and National Australia topping the value turnover list. The stock of media group News Corp was also favoured by local investors after its ADRs were supported in New York on Monday.
Dealers said despite the rise investors remained cautious with the principal concern being the inexorable rise of the Wall Street market.
"When the market falls 70 points people get a bit bruised and battered and a little bit tentative. They have their feelers out and are just taking bites here and there," Atkinson said.
One issue out of step with the market was beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil whose shares continued their recent downward move following a profit downgrade in mid-November.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures activity remained subdued but options business picked up from Monday's low levels as traders renewed their interest in major resource issues BHP and WMC.

In other local markets, Australian bonds ended little changed from Monday's levels as domestic markets took a more cautionary stance in view of recent gyrations and ahead of key economic data later this week.
By the close 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.37 percent, down 0.1 percentage points from Monday's close.
The Australian dollar kept a grip on most of its 1/2 cent of offshore gains but did little else in a consolidative session.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT) the currency was quoted at US$0.8015/20 having risen from US$0.7983/88 late on Monday.
